title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from §41, §46 and §47). Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite π1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}, with generators ℓ0, ℓ1, ℓ∞. Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a profinite group generated by an involution σ∞ and an element ρ of order 3, so it behaves like (Z/2 * Z/3)^ ≅ PSL2(Z)^. It contains Π̂_{0,3} as a normal subgroup of index 6 (the S_3-extension), with ℓ0 = ε0^2 where ε0 = σ∞ρ (next page uses this).

There is a second homomorphism φ̂ : Π̂ → Ŝ^+, defined by ℓ0 ↦ ε0, ℓ1 ↦ σ∞, ℓ∞ ↦ ρ^{-1}. This is the 'orbifold filling' map. It sends the λ-line to the j-line orbifold, with cone points of order ∞, 2, 3 at the images of 0, 1, ∞.

The automorphism u. u ∈ M^{!~}_{0,3} is a Grothendieck-style 'automorphisme à lacets' of Π̂ commuting externally with S_3. It extends to Ŝ^+ by u(σ∞) = int(β0)σ∞ and u(ρ) = int(α0)ρ, with β0 = f^{-1}β and α0 = f^{-1}α. The question is when u commutes externally with φ̂, i.e. when there is λ in Ŝ^+ with φ̂∘u = int(λ)∘u∘φ̂. This is the condition singling out the subgroup M^{!≈}_{0,3} and the homomorphism to M^{≈}_{0,3}.

Step 1 (x = ℓ0, prev. page). u(ℓ0) = int(f^{-1})ℓ0^μ, so φ̂u(ℓ0) = int(φ̂(f)^{-1})ε0^μ. Also uφ̂(ℓ0) = u(ε0) = int(f^{-1})ε0^μ.
- Hence φ̂(f)λf^{-1} centralizes ε0^μ.
- The marginal NB records that φ̂(f) need not lie in Π̂, so this centralizer must be computed in Ŝ^+, not in Π̂.
- The centralizer of ε0^μ (a parabolic element of infinite order) is the closure of ⟨ε0⟩. So φ̂(f)λf^{-1} = ε0^r with r ∈ Ẑ, i.e. (6): λ = φ̂(f)^{-1}ε0^r f.

Step 2 (x = ℓ1). u(ℓ1) = int(f1^{-1})ℓ1^μ with f1^{-1} = gρ(f)^{-1}, where ρ(·) = int(ρ). Since μ is odd, σ∞^μ = σ∞, so φ̂u(ℓ1) = int(φ̂(f1)^{-1})σ∞. Also uφ̂(ℓ1) = u(σ∞) = int(β0)σ∞.
- So φ̂(f1)λβ0 centralizes σ∞. Its centralizer is {1, σ∞}, giving φ̂(f1^{-1}) = λβ0σ∞^i with i ∈ Z/2.
- Substituting (6) and β0 = f^{-1}β gives φ̂(gρ(f)^{-1}) = φ̂(f)^{-1}ε0^r β σ∞^i.
- Hence φ̂(f g ρ(f)^{-1}) = ε0^r β σ∞^i.
- Since g = α0ρ(α0)^{-1} and α = fα0, we have f g ρ(f)^{-1} = αρ(α)^{-1} = ξ.

Result (stated as a theorem on the next page). u commutes externally with φ̂ if and only if φ̂(ξ) = ε0^r β σ∞^i for some r ∈ Ẑ and i ∈ Z/2. The pair (r, i) transforms as r' = r − n, i' = i + n under the ambiguity (α, β, f) ↦ ℓ0^n(α, β, f).

Purpose. This is a compatibility condition between Grothendieck's 'loop-equation' description of GT-like automorphisms of π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) and the two maps relating the λ-line to the j-line / PSL2 orbifold: the S_3-quotient inclusion and the cone-point filling map. It is a step toward determining how the 'Teichmüller tower' groups act on (Z/2*Z/3)^.
errors: Intermediate inverse slip: from φ̂u(ℓ1) = int(φ̂(f1)^{-1})σ∞ = int(λβ0)σ∞ the correct consequence is that φ̂(f1)λβ0 centralizes σ∞. Grothendieck writes φ̂(f1)^{-1}λβ0 instead, and also writes int(φ̂(f1)^{-1})σ∞ = int(φ̂(f1))σ∞. His final relation φ̂(f1^{-1}) = λβ0σ∞^i is nevertheless correct, because σ∞^{-i} = σ∞^i, so the slips cancel.

Gap: the facts Centr_{Ŝ^+}(ε0^μ) = closure⟨ε0⟩ and Centr_{Ŝ^+}(σ∞) = {1, σ∞} in the profinite free product (Z/2*Z/3)^ are asserted without proof. They are true (known results on centralizers in profinite free products) but non-trivial in the profinite setting.
In (4), λ is first stated to lie in Π̂_{0,3}. The marginal NB corrects this implicitly: λ must be allowed in Ŝ^+.
Notational inconsistency: (6) uses ε0^r, while the next page restates it as λ = φ̂(f)^{-1} l0^r f, where l0 = ε0^2 in Ŝ^+. The correct form is ε0^r.

ideas.what: Filling map π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) → (Z/2*Z/3)^ (cusp, order 2, order 3) compared with the index-6 inclusion Γ(2)-type ⊂ PSL2, both relating the λ-line to the j-line orbifold
ideas.modern_name: λ-line vs j-line (M_{0,4}/S_3 ≅ M_{1,1} orbifold), profinite PSL2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; profinite/Galois-theoretic use by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower in general terms; this specific computation is not known to be published

ideas.what: Criterion for an inertia-preserving S_3-compatible automorphism (parameters α, β, f, ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}) to commute externally with the filling map: φ̂(ξ) = ε0^r β σ∞^i
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of GT-type automorphisms with the action on profinite PSL2(Z) / genus-one (M_{1,1}) conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related GT/genus-one work: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), Nakamura–Schneps

ideas.what: Elimination of the conjugating element λ via centralizers of the parabolic ε0 and the involution σ∞ in the profinite free product

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives an explicit equation characterizing which 'automorphismes à lacets' of Π̂_{0,3} are compatible with the orbifold filling map Π̂_{0,3} → (Z/2*Z/3)^. This compares the λ-line → j-line S_3-quotient with the cone-point filling. It is a genus-0 → M_{1,1} compatibility condition in the spirit of the extra relations later imposed on GT (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps' variant of GT). Whether this exact condition, in Grothendieck's (α, β, f, ξ) parametrization, coincides with or differs from known relations seems undocumented.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Checking whether this condition holds automatically for all of GT (or Gal(Q̄/Q)), or cuts out a subgroup, would situate Grothendieck's M^{!≈}_{0,3} relative to GT, its LNS genus-one variant and Nakamura–Schneps' subgroups. That bears on how many independent relations the 'Teichmüller tower' requires.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, essentially correct computation within Grothendieck's unpublished loop-equation framework. It produces an explicit compatibility criterion between GT-type automorphisms and the λ-line → j-line filling map. The theme is close to known GT/M_{1,1} literature, so this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a surprising result.
transcription_corrections: Every occurrence of 'φ̂(y)' and 'ρ(y)' should read 'φ̂(f)' and 'ρ(f)'; the handwritten f was misread as y.
The centralizer is Centr_{Ŝ^+}(ε0^μ) or Centr(ε0^H), with H = μ. The marginal NB indicates it is taken in Ŝ^+, not Π̂_{0,3}.
'f_1^{-1} = g ρ(f^{-1})', i.e. g ρ(f)^{-1}; the crossed-out text precedes it.
The final exponent 'σ∞^{β[?]α}' should read σ∞^{α̇} (i ∈ Z/2Z); the 'β' is a misreading.
'ce que signifie' should read 'ce qui signifie'.
